name: Iran nuclear programme
summary: IAEA cannot verify Iran's 60%-enriched uranium; Iran says inspections cannot resume while under military threat
state: An IAEA report circulated on 13 Nov urged Iran to restore inspector access and said the agency cannot verify whether the underground Isfahan enrichment plant holds nuclear material (Al Jazeera). Its last estimate of uranium enriched up to 60% is 440.9kg; Iran said monitoring talks cannot proceed while it faces explicit threats, and the IAEA Board meets this week (Political.org). No new strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or evidence of weaponisation was found as of 18 Nov.
for_you: There is no direct risk to the public outside the region. Travellers should follow FCDO advice, which currently warns against travel to Iran.
rubric_hit: 60% enrichment and inspector access curtailed = Watch

sources.title: Al Jazeera — UN watchdog calls on Iran to reopen nuclear facilities to inspection
Political.org — Iran tells UN nuclear watchdog monitoring talks cannot proceed while under military threat

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
